title: Any tips for making a great UI in Godot using AI?
author: NicNacksTheSixSnax
selftext:
Hi All.

One thing I’ve always struggled with is UI. Since it’s so subjective it’s always been a pain for me to get right. 

Anyone want to share tips or prompts for how they get good looking UI’s in their games? 

Thanks!

comments.author: revel911
comments.body: The biggest thing is just find examples of what you like , lots of examples. Then with something like chat gpt refine those into a single golden style, then use to build a fleshed out design system continuously telling it to unify any parameters that are out of form. Once done, have your game use that as the basis.

replies.author: NicNacksTheSixSnax
replies.body: I like this a lot. Will definitely give it a try. I would like to have templates a real artist can edit/modify/build off from.

replies.author: revel911
replies.body: You can then look at the Figma mcp to import / export, that will put as an editable style .

replies.author: revel911
replies.body: You can then look at the Figma mcp to import / export, that will put as an editable style .

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
A lot of the UI is fine-tuning. Prompting is a slow way to do that. Go in yourself and manually adjust fonts, sizes, margins, colors, etc. way faster than telling AI to fix things.

Get it close with AI, fine tune it the rest of the way by hand.

replies.author: NicNacksTheSixSnax
replies.body:
Agreed. I do eventually want to do this but I want to achieve a good standard before tweaking personally. If that makes sense?

Right now all I have is standard Godot boxes and buttons.

comments.author: Material-Watercress1
comments.body: Ask the AI to come up with a video game themed design system and then iterate on examples with it until you get something that feels right. By default, every UI that it makes will look like AI web app slop. If you have it come up with a design e.g., pixel graphics, it will help keep it on a better track

replies.author: NicNacksTheSixSnax
replies.body:
True. I have had it make pixel art for units in my game. I didn’t think to have it do pixel art for the UI as well. I thought it would be too distracting. 

Appreciate your response.

comments.author: OakNLeaf
comments.body: I have a style guide that is very detailed. It goes through about everything I need in terms of the colors/fonts/designes/etc that I want it to ensure is always used when developing. It's gone well so far for me.

replies.author: NicNacksTheSixSnax
replies.body: How did you develop your style guide? Pre-exisiting examples that you like or via prompt descriptions?

replies.author: OakNLeaf
replies.body: I have a template I made based on other style guides I have seen/used at my job and other projects. Pretty much I have Claude review the styleguide and if it tells me what areas are unclear and what it understands from my style guide. I go back and forth with Claude probably 30 or 40 times until i think it understands it completely how I want it.
